note: Evidence is attached to the exact tested commit and workflow/job. Browser, unit and native records are scoped to the explicit stable IDs shown. Dynamic QR/barcode browser evidence is read from qa-results/qr-barcode-reader-audit.json after the live audit; blocked checks are preserved rather than counted as passes. Manifest membership and execution-matrix classification are never treated as per-tool native test evidence.

audits.step: Verify all 93 Celebrations tools on a mobile browser
audits.notes: All 93 exact catalogue IDs were routed through the mobile browser audit. This does not establish every visible control, boundary case, token, backend, offline or native check.

audits.step: Verify local File workspace workflows in the browser
audits.notes: Six explicit routes and representative local file/folder workflows were exercised. This is not exhaustive control or boundary-input coverage.

audits.step: Verify Zip any file compression and extraction in the browser
audits.notes: The browser test verified multi-file and single-file archive creation, CRC-checked reads, extraction round-trip and no application API writes.
Dedicated sandbox browser route tested with local audio/tag fixtures and responsive viewports. It does not cover the rest of the Audio category or native implementations.
Unit tests cover sandbox rights/review gates, metadata preservation, decoded-audio limits and the exact Web route/legacy aliases. No broader Audio-family claim is made.

audits.step: Run Kotlin unit tests and Android lint
audits.notes: The Android test enumerates all 93 expected IDs and verifies independent Kotlin operation parsing, then exercises representative invitation, page, quiz, memory and countdown outputs. This is not 93 separate full UI/device acceptance tests.
